result.title: ACROSSVAM3.0: Resource-Bounded 4D Scene Construction and Adaptive Surface Association
result.summary: Combining video generation, dynamic reconstruction and monocular SLAM requires consistent coordinates, explicit handling of missing outputs and predictable memory use. We present AcrossVAM3.0, an offline system that converts text, images or monocular RGB video into a versioned point representation. Frozen components run sequentially on one GPU; map corrections update cameras, points and trajectories together. The coordination layer adds no neural parameters. Three fresh input-mode runs completed with a maximum sampled task-process-tree GPU footprint of 17.14 GB. In a frozen 16-scene video suite, every scene yielded a 4D reconstruction and 15 yielded a non-empty SLAM map. Strict cross-window matching reduced local surface error but lost long-range track coverage on TAP-Vid-DAVIS. We therefore developed multi-hypothesis adaptive surface chaining (MHAC), which retains several candidate matches and an explicit missing state. After selection on disjoint development data, MHAC improved Average Jaccard over a position-only baseline by 0.1394 on a frozen ten-video holdout (95% bootstrap interval [0.1074,0.1689]). Across 265 RoboTAP videos, the mean paired gain was 0.0610 ([0.0510,0.0715]), with 215 wins, one tie and 49 losses. These results support resource-bounded scene construction and an external tracking gain under the tested protocol. They do not establish metric scale, semantic identity or high-fidelity novel-view rendering.

AI.brief_summary: 提出离线系统 AcrossVAM3.0，将文本、图像或单目视频转换为可版本化的点表示：冻结组件在同一 GPU 上顺序运行，地图修正统一更新相机、点与轨迹，并以多假设自适应表面链接（MHAC）保留多个候选匹配和显式缺失状态，在 TAP-Vid-DAVIS 与 RoboTAP 视频上评测跟踪增益与 GPU 占用。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「多候选假设＋显式缺失状态」的关联机制与资源受限预算设计，可能为 latent 推理中的多假设维护、视觉证据缺失时的状态表达及计算成本核算提供参照，可供核查其是否可迁移。
